trust_decision.summary: Which value an atomic validation error may render: the confirm validation's atomic path puts the confirmed field's value (an atomic_ref to the stored column when the field is not being changed) into the InvalidAttribute error, while the non-atomic path renders only the caller-supplied confirmation value; redaction is applied only when the field is marked sensitive and the redaction config is enabled.

landing_point.why: The summary names Ash.Resource.Validation.Confirm and the atomic mismatch error, and error_value in atomic/3 is the only value placed in that error.

fix_sites.entry_point: Public API: an update action with `validate confirm(field, confirmation)` run atomically via Ash.update / Ash.bulk_update (require_atomic? or atomic upgrade)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The compare validation is a separate built-in; a {:ref, field} comparison bound reads like a declared threshold, not a confirmed secret, and an existing test only asserts on the message text, so a solver can argue that rendering the bound's value is intended behaviour.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Non-sensitive validation errors must still carry the user-supplied value (error.value == input), and sensitive ones must render **redacted**. An over-broad fix that blanks or redacts every confirm/compare error value breaks this. Atomic compare with {:ref, field} must still produce a 'must be less than or equal to ...' message.

O6_input_shapes: field not changing in the update (value = atomic_ref of stored column)
field changing in the update (value = fetched change)
confirmation given as argument vs attribute (atomic_ref fallback)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Atomic compare with a {:ref, other_field} bound puts atomic_ref(other_field) into the error vars, so the rendered message interpolates the other field's stored value. The non-atomic path renders the field name through describe/format_value.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is a different validation module, and the value is a 'bound' in vars rather than error.value; this looks like a neighbouring feature that was fixed separately (the {:ref} resolution commit).
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: Same package, different file (lib/ash/resource/validation/compare.ex vs confirm.ex). Same pattern at compare.ex:153,167,181,193,206 via atomic_value at compare.ex:376-382; non-atomic contrast at compare.ex:347-348.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A multi-attribute validation whose atomic error value is atomic_ref of an attribute other than the one the caller supplied
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: present.ex already puts atomic_ref(first attribute) into value with no should_redact? check, so a maintainer could write the same thing for a paired-field validation.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: An atomic 'changing from/to' error that renders ref(field) (the old stored value) instead of atomic_ref(field)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: atomic_condition already mixes ref (stored) and atomic_ref (new) at changing.ex:208-209, so swapping them in the error is a one-token slip.

O9_family: CWE-209 information exposure through error message (stored value rendered in validation error)

O10_build.toolchain: Elixir/Erlang OTP with mix (deps fetched once via mix deps.get)
O10_build.project_tests: test/actions/validation_test.exs (sensitive value redaction describe block, ETS data layer, Ash.bulk_update atomic cases); test/resource/validation/compare_test.exs:515-560 atomic {:ref} path

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Wrap error_value in Ash.Helpers.redact unconditionally (or only when sensitive), instead of rendering the caller-supplied confirmation value as the non-atomic path does.

out_of_scope_notes: lib/ash/resource/validation/match.ex:154 builds an error value with no maybe_redact for sensitive attributes; this is a separate redaction concern, not pursued.
